extra.message: Single static shared-secret header gates multiple RCE-class internal endpoints with no rate limiting — Anyone who obtains or brute-forces INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN gets direct unauthenticated access to pickle/eval/SSTI/XXE RCE-class endpoints [verified: _wrk_gate is a plain non-constant-time string comparison against a single static token with no rate limiting, guarding pickle/eval/SSTI/XXE RCE endpoints.]

Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on request-controlled data — Arbitrary code execution on the server via a crafted pickle payload [verified: pickle.loads runs on raw request-controlled bytes with no allow-list or restricted unpickler; only gate is a static header check.]

Code injection via eval() on user-supplied expression — Arbitrary Python code execution by escaping the restricted eval sandbox [verified: eval() on user expr with __builtins__ restricted only, a well-known bypassable sandbox (e.g. via ().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()).]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 Template(string) construction — Arbitrary code execution via Jinja2 template gadget chains (e.g. object introspection to os.popen) [verified: Jinja2 Template built via string concat of raw GET param and rendered, enabling classic SSTI/RCE gadget chains.]

Arbitrary file write via path traversal on export storage endpoint — Write attacker-controlled file contents outside the intended export directory, potentially overwriting application code or planting a webshell for RCE [verified: name from request.GET is joined into BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no traversal sanitization before write_bytes(request.body).]

Hardcoded/weak fallback Django SECRET_KEY — If deployed with the default or example key, an attacker who knows the fallback string can forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, and password-reset tokens, leading to account takeover and access to confidential client/matter data. [verified: SECRET_KEY hardcoded fallback at settings.py:9-12 is used whenever DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset, enabling session/CSRF/token forgery if deployed unchanged.]

Insecure defaults for DEBUG and SECRET_KEY — Verbose Django debug pages leaking source/config, or session/CSRF forgery via a known default SECRET_KEY [verified: settings.py:9-13 has SECRET_KEY and DEBUG both default to insecure values absent env vars, a genuinely present misconfiguration on the default deployment path.]

Sensitive token/PII exposed in ops response — Disclosure of a partner sync token and PII (SSN-like value) to any caller of the endpoint, independent of the case_id parameter, enabling downstream credential/PII abuse [verified: Endpoint unconditionally returns a live-looking secret token and SSN-like PII regardless of case_id, gated only by the weak static token.]

NoSQL injection via unvalidated pymongo query filter — Unauthorized data read from the ops MongoDB collection, potential $where JS execution enabling further compromise [verified: payload.get('filter', payload) passed unfiltered to pymongo find_one, allowing operator injection with no validation.]

XXE via lxml parser with entity resolution and network access enabled — Local file disclosure, SSRF to internal services, and billion-laughs DoS via crafted XML [verified: XMLParser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False parses raw request.body, enabling XXE.]

DEBUG defaults to True in settings and example env file — Unauthenticated attackers who trigger any server error see full Django debug tracebacks: source snippets, local variable values (potentially including session/user objects, DB rows, secrets), installed apps, and settings — enabling further exploitation of a legal case management system holding privileged client data. [verified: DEBUG defaults to true when DJANGO_DEBUG is unset, exposing verbose tracebacks; confirmed present in code at settings.py:13.]

Unhandled input-driven exception on API endpoint leaks debug page due to DEBUG defaulting True — Any holder of a valid API key (or, if DEBUG stays True in production, any user reaching a similarly unguarded code path) can force a stack-trace disclosure revealing internal source paths, settings values, and request/environment details, aiding further attacks. [verified: DEBUG defaults to true when DJANGO_DEBUG unset (legal_firm/settings.py:13), and matter_list performs int(request.GET.get("limit")) with no exception handling, so any API-key holder sending limit=abc triggers an uncaught ValueError rendering Django's verbose debug page with stack trace/settings/env.]

Reflected XSS in ops banner preview endpoint — Attacker-controlled script execution in the browser of anyone who opens a crafted ops preview link [verified: copyline GET param concatenated directly into HTML response with no escaping, reflected XSS.]

Mass assignment of privileged fields from request JSON — Attacker can escalate is_admin/role/credit_limit fields in the returned workspace object [verified: workset.update(change_set) merges attacker JSON directly onto privileged fields (role, is_admin, credit_limit) with no field allow-list.]

Unvalidated ledger amount/state manipulation — Anyone holding the internal ops token can forge arbitrary balance changes or force approval state on a financial/matter ledger record, bypassing intended business workflow checks [verified: amount and state taken directly from client payload and applied to ledger balance/state with no validation, allowing negative-amount balance inflation and forced state.]

Sensitive data (Authorization bearer token) written to logs — Credential/token leakage to anyone with log read access, enabling account takeover or lateral movement [verified: logger.warning logs full raw body and Authorization header verbatim, persisting secrets into logs.]

CORS misconfiguration: reflected Origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious site can issue credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses, enabling cross-origin data theft against authenticated sessions [verified: Origin header reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.]

Disabled TLS certificate validation on outbound HTTPS request — Enables man-in-the-middle interception/tampering of outbound server-to-server traffic [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() used for outbound urlopen, disabling certificate validation.]

CSV/Formula Injection in Audit Log Export — Arbitrary formula/DDE command execution or data exfiltration on the machine of a firm admin who opens the exported audit log CSV, using attacker-controlled client/matter names as the injection vector. [verified: description is written to CSV via csv.writer with no escaping of leading =/+/-/@ characters, and description embeds user-controlled fields like client.name/matter.reference; opening in Excel/Sheets can trigger formula execution.]

CSV formula injection in matter/deadline/document export — A malicious matter/deadline/document title or tag containing a spreadsheet formula (e.g. =cmd|'/c calc'!A0 or a DDE payload) executes when a firm admin/attorney opens the exported CSV in Excel/Sheets, potentially leading to data exfiltration or command execution on the reviewer's machine. [verified: _csv_response() sanitizes only the filename (cases/views_admin.py:223); matter/deadline/document title/reference/tags fields are written verbatim via csv.writer.writerow() with no leading =/+/-/@ neutralization, so a crafted title triggers formula execution when opened in Excel/Sheets.]

CSV formula injection (CSV/Excel macro injection) in document/matter export — A client-portal user can plant a formula string in a document title/tag that firm staff later export to CSV; opening the file in Excel/Sheets executes the formula, enabling remote command execution, credential/data exfiltration, or phishing against staff. [verified: ClientUploadForm.title (cases/forms.py:186) is client-portal-controlled free text bound directly to Document.title with no formula-character stripping, and document_export (views_admin.py:303-316) writes it to CSV unescaped, so a client can plant a payload that executes when staff export and open the file.]

Brute-forceable identity verifier with no rate limiting — An attacker who can reach the gated endpoint can brute-force the 4-digit verifier for either handle to obtain a successful identity confirmation [verified: 4-digit verifier checked via plain != against a tiny hardcoded keyspace with no rate limiting, brute-forceable in ≤10000 requests.]

Weak PRNG used for token/nonce generation — Predictable tokens if reused for auth/reset nonces, enabling brute-force or prediction attacks [verified: random.choice (non-CSPRNG) used to generate a security-sounding code/token.]

Security headers explicitly disabled (CSP/X-XSS-Protection) — Removes defense-in-depth browser protections, increasing impact of any XSS reachable through this response path [verified: Response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection: 0 and empty CSP, removing defense-in-depth headers.]
